name: Unverified swap contract pays its Uniswap V3 callback to any caller-named pool
summary: The unverified swap contract 0xd132b6e4 that 0x929d13c8 deployed for its traders exposes 0x14776a7c(pool, recipient, tokenIn, minOut, amountIn), which pulls tokenIn from the caller and calls swap on the caller-named pool, and its uniswapV3SwapCallback pays the token the pool reports as owed from the contract's own balance to whatever pool calls back, without checking that the pool is a real Uniswap V3 pool. The attacker deployed a fake token and a fake pool, called 0x14776a7c with 1 fake token in, and had the fake pool call back claiming 3,131.11 DAI, the contract's whole DAI balance, which it forwarded to the attacker.
notes: Mechanism from the exploit trace, as the contract is unverified: the callback (0xfa461e33) transferred 3,131.11 DAI to the fake pool 0xe69ac220 that the caller had named, and the entry also sent the caller's fake-token fee to the deployer 0x929d13c8. The DAI had sat in the contract since block 68192388, when a trader's 3,876.71 DAI swap output was forwarded only in part (745.60 DAI).

campaign.mjs over all calls into the contract from its deployment to the chain head: the 233 earlier exercises of 0x14776a7c and the callback are traders swapping their own tokens through real pools with nothing paid to the caller; the only later one is 0x3128a77f's fake-pool call taking 1 USDT0 (0x7a8e5a9f, block 91700169). The contract is direct and unchanged since deployment; its admin changes (createAdmin, deleteAdmin, changeSupperAdmin) only replace holders of roles the exploit did not use.
Loss is the contract's DAI and USDT0 outflow to the fake pools, priced by loss.mjs.
